questions.def: Frankly is a comment adverb used to express an honest opinion.
questions.question: ___, I think the movie was boring.

questions.def: Luckily is a comment adverb showing a positive viewpoint about the weather.
questions.question: ___, the weather is beautiful today.

questions.def: Surely is a comment adverb expressing a degree of certainty.
questions.question: ___, he will be late again.

questions.def: Generally speaking is a phrase to introduce a general viewpoint.
questions.question: ___ speaking, I don't agree with his decision.

questions.def: Surprisingly indicates the speaker's surprise at the situation.
questions.question: ___, I didn't expect to see you here!

questions.def: Clearly indicates that something is obvious from the speaker's viewpoint.
questions.question: ___, he doesn't know what he is doing.

questions.def: Personally expresses a personal opinion or viewpoint.
questions.question: ___, I think we should leave now.

questions.def: Honestly expresses the speaker's sincere opinion about the food.
questions.question: ___, the food was delicious.

questions.def: Sadly expresses the speaker's sadness about the situation.
questions.question: ___, he lost his job.

questions.def: Apparently means according to what one has heard or seen.
questions.question: ___, it's going to rain later.

questions.def: Certainly expresses a strong belief or conviction.
questions.question: ___, he is a good student.

questions.def: Wisely expresses that something is a sensible or good idea.
questions.question: ___, it's better to stay home.

questions.def: Undoubtedly means without doubt; certainly.
questions.question: ___, she is very kind.

questions.def: Seriously expresses a strong opinion or belief.
questions.question: ___, he should apologize.

questions.def: More formally, use "I hope" instead of "Hopefully" in this construction.
questions.question: Hopefully, the weather will be sunny tomorrow.

questions.def: Fortunately means by good luck.
questions.question: ___, I found my keys.

questions.def: Evidently means plainly or obviously.
questions.question: ___, this is a difficult problem.

questions.def: Regrettably expresses regret about something.
questions.question: ___, I made a mistake.

questions.def: "Frank" should be "Frankly", comment adverb.
questions.question: Frank, I don't think that is a good idea.

questions.def: Truly means in a truthful way; honestly.
questions.question: ___, he didn't want to go.

questions.def: Admittedly means used to introduce a statement that is true.
questions.question: ___, the game was exciting.

questions.def: Strictly speaking means in the exact sense of the word.
questions.question: ___ speaking, the project was a success.

questions.def: Normally means usually or regularly.
questions.question: ___, I wake up at 7 am.

questions.def: Gladly means in a willing or cheerful way.
questions.question: ___, I am happy to help you.

questions.def: Incredibly expresses astonishment or disbelief.
questions.question: ___, I can't believe it's over.

questions.def: Use 'Honestly' as a comment adverb to express your true opinion.
questions.question: ___, the movie wasn't as good as the book.

questions.def: 'Personally' is a viewpoint adverb indicating a personal opinion.
questions.question: ___, I think we should go home now.

questions.def: Use 'Carefully' as a comment adverb to advise caution.
questions.question: Careful, I think the paint is still wet.

questions.def: 'Fortunately' expresses the speaker's attitude about the situation.
questions.question: ___, I found my keys.

questions.def: 'Surprisingly' shows the speaker's reaction to an event.
questions.question: ___, he didn't even say thank you.
